sources.title: Manage Syncs
sources.summary: CalendarBridge describes directional source-to-destination copying; bidirectional groups consist of directional pairs. Destination copies do not edit originals. Controls cover replicated fields, filters, status and manual rescans. Deleting a sync leaves existing placeholders. Troubleshooting mentions a bounded date window and organization approval.
candidateIntentTerms: stop calendar sync keep copied events
boundaries: Private flag and OAuth-password statements are not adopted as universal provider facts.
Suggested manual duplicate deletion is not imported into Cloud advice.

sources.title: How to get a .ics URL for your calendar
sources.summary: The page distinguishes source-only feeds from account connections, covers provider link retrieval, and contrasts imported files with subscriptions. It also promotes a combined feed product.
boundaries: Provider instructions here are secondary to Apple/Google/Microsoft documentation.
A literal .ics suffix is not a universal validity test.
Do not republish a private calendar merely to troubleshoot.
Its own provider sections mention restricted-detail feeds, so the final exclusivity claim needs independent evidence.
No Cloud support for every listed provider or generated aggregate feed inferred.

sources.title: About Syncing
sources.summary: Describes one-way copying rules, source-authoritative edits, avoidance of recopy loops, optional copied details, and different source-dependent update cadences. Claims no event-count limit.
candidateIntentTerms: one way versus two way calendar sync
boundaries: Cadence and capacity are CalendarBridge claims, not measured results or Cloud guarantees.
An event-count limit and a date-window limit are different dimensions; do not equate unrestricted count with unlimited history.

sources.title: Calendar & Scheduling Tools for People with Multiple Calendars
sources.summary: Separates combined viewing, calendar copying, booking pages and scheduling assistance as different solutions. Discusses work/personal visibility, multiple accounts, and detail controls. FAQs distinguish original events from copies and periodic versus source-triggered updates.
candidateIntentTerms: busy time without private event details
boundaries: Security, compliance, storage, pricing and testimonial claims are unverified publisher assertions.
Booking pages and AI scheduling are not inferred Cloud features.
No subscriptions, trials or account changes performed.

taskMappings.coverage: Already explicit in full current bodies. Preserve both the no-automatic-busy-bridge warning and the actual device-mirror disclosure.
taskMappings.suggestedChange: No new route. Optional one-sentence diagnostic: identify original versus destination before editing a mirrored entry.

taskMappings.task: Keep personal appointment details out of workplace availability
taskMappings.coverage: Existing guide already has an approved manual busy-block example and recipient-side verification.
taskMappings.suggestedChange: No duplicate privacy-block guide. Preserve the distinction between manual approved arrangement and unsupported automatic masking.

taskMappings.task: Find a feed, import a snapshot, or connect an editable account
taskMappings.coverage: Current bodies already distinguish account/feed/import and handle exposed addresses and timing.
taskMappings.suggestedChange: Keep Google own-use guidance. Only add provider-specific retrieval steps after reading that provider; no thin URL-suffix guide.

taskMappings.task: Explain stale or missing calendar data without destructive cleanup
taskMappings.coverage: Current bodies cover identity, ownership, permission, source visibility and safe disposable tests.
taskMappings.suggestedChange: Optional sync-guide checklist: if a separate copying service is involved, examine its configured filters and covered dates. Do not invent equivalent Cloud switches.

taskMappings.task: Stop an external copy relationship while handling remaining destination records
taskMappings.coverage: Revocation guide covers grants, feeds and retained exports; neither reviewed guide provides a dedicated third-party integration offboarding procedure.
taskMappings.suggestedChange: Candidate new task, not yet publication-ready: distinguish disabling automation, revoking provider authorization and reviewing existing copies. Require provider permission-revocation docs and native Cloud disconnect inspection before any Cloud-specific instructions.

newGapAssessment.candidate: Disconnecting a calendar integration without confusing live authorization with retained copies
newGapAssessment.status: Scoped candidate after index check and eight relevant body reads; not a verified product workflow and not a claim of exhaustive corpus semantic review.
newGapAssessment.nextEvidence: Official Google/Microsoft/Apple connected-app revocation instructions; actual Cloud disconnect data-retention behavior read-only inspection; independent check of any proposed destructive cleanup.

crossPageCautions: Manage Syncs gives general near-minute language; older About Syncing explicitly differentiates source cadence. Keep source type and publisher date attached; do not present a guaranteed interval.
Manage Syncs mentions a finite default date window while About Syncing claims no event-count limit. These may coexist; do not conflate them or claim unlimited history.
Provider privacy and authorization behavior must be sourced to the actual provider before publication.
